name: Weak-field gravitational lensing focal length f = b^2 c^2/(4GM) (Einstein light deflection 4GM/(b c^2), source at infinity)

source.located: Einstein's weak-field light deflection alpha = 4GM/(c^2 b) (A. Einstein, Ann. Phys. 49 (1916) 769; pre-arXiv classic) and the solar-gravitational-lens focus b^2/(2 r_g) ~ 547.8 AU (S.G. Turyshev and V.T. published_statement: NOT READ at source this stage. The textbook form, which is what the tree uses and what was re-derived here (R1-R2): a light ray passing a mass M at impact parameter b in the weak field is deflected toward the mass by alpha = 4GM/(c^2 b) (twice the Newtonian corpuscular value); rays from a source at infinity at impact parameter b therefore cross the optical axis at z = b/alpha = b^2 c^2/(4GM). For the Sun at b = R_sun the published focus is ~547.8 AU (WebSearch summary of Toth & Turyshev; NOT READ), and since f grows with b the lens has a focal LINE, not a point (same summary: 'a gravitational lens has spherical aberration ... no single focal point but a focal line').
published_hypotheses: H1 weak field: |Phi|/c^2 = GM/(c^2 r) << 1 along the path (linearised metric); the result is first order in GM/(c^2 b). (Stated in every restatement; re-derived here as the Born integral R1.)
H2 small deflection and straight-line (Born) path: the deflection is integrated along the unperturbed ray.
H3 spherically symmetric lens with the ray outside the matter (b >= R), so the exterior field is that of a point mass (Birkhoff).

H4 geometric optics: light follows null geodesics, i.e. wavelength << the lens scale 4GM/c^2 (the published SGL work treats this with wave optics; NOT READ here, the on-axis wave gain is derived here in R9).
H5 source at infinity (plane wave incident); f is the focal point of that beam. A source at finite distance D_s focuses at f D_s/(D_s - f) (thin lens).
H6 thin lens: f >> b, so the deflection is accumulated over a region small compared with the path.
H7 GR value of the PPN parameter gamma = 1; in the PPN framework alpha = (1+gamma)/2 * 4GM/(c^2 b).
H8 (for the Sun, published SGL work; search summary, NOT READ) the plasma of the solar corona is negligible at optical wavelengths but not at radio.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED -- geometric optics (H4), at spec.py:57-72 (the 'focal' column including '10 km asteroid ... 1580 ly', spec.py:72), spec.py:188-194 (DOES[0], DOES[4]) and specthm.py:1315-1332 (SR1 statement prints the asteroid row). The tree's claims are phrased for NULL GEODESICS (specthm.py:1313 'a NULL congruence') and as geometry they are exact; but the tree reads the focus as physical focusing ('a lens', 'the Sun already does exactly this'). For the 10 km asteroid 4GM/c^2 = 6.68e-12 m, so at 500 nm the wave parameter w = 8 pi G M/(c^2 lambda) = 8.4e-5 and the on-axis gain is pi w/(1 - e^{-pi w}) = 1.00013 (R9): no light focus at any wavelength longer than ~1e-11 m. Earth (4GM/c^2 = 1.8 cm) is geometric in the optical but not at cm radio (w = 11 at 1 cm). The Sun (w = 7.4e10 at 500 nm, gain 2.3e11) is deep in the geometric regime, so every load-bearing use (S-1 witness, SR1, R5-S) is unaffected.

WEAKENED -- vacuum along the ray, at specthm.py:1311-1312 ('impact parameter b >= the lens radius, so the congruence passes through vacuum') and 1317 ('through vacuum'), with the Sun at b = R_sun (spec.py:65, 235; specthm.py:1322). b = R_sun is the photospheric radius and the grazing ray traverses the solar atmosphere; the tree names no frequency condition. For null geodesics the coronal matter is ordinary (T_kk > 0, NEC/WEC/DEC hold) and gravitationally negligible, so the geodesic claim survives; for light, per 1811.06515 (search summary, NOT READ) the corona pushes the radio focal area outward and leaves optical unaffected. The magnitude was NOT computed here (it needs a coronal density model that was not read).

RELABELLED -- source at infinity vs 'source outside the focal length', at specthm.py:1310 (hypothesis) against specthm.py:1318 ('the source-at-infinity focus'). The formula is the D_s -> infinity focus; for finite D_s > f the conjugate point lies at f D_s/(D_s - f) > f (R2, sympy). The tree correctly draws the consequence that f(R_lens) is the MINIMUM range (specthm.py:1322-1323). Also semantic: with the source at infinity f is the focal point of the incident plane wavefront (a focal point of a null hypersurface), a 'conjugate point' only in the limit of a two-point conjugate pair. No conclusion moves.

EXTENDED (not an error) -- positive lens mass dropped in concentric.py: concentric.py:68, 305, 345 print f = b^2/4m for a NEGATIVE Plummer core of mass -m (concentric.py:42-47), against the positive-mass hypothesis at spec.py:190 and specthm.py:1308. The source result is attractive/azimuthal focusing. Re-derived here (R3): 1/f_az = alpha/b = 4M/b^2 and 1/f_rad = d(alpha)/db = -4M/b^2, so for M < 0 the RADIAL direction focuses at b^2/(4|M|) -- the same det A = 0 distance, consistent with composite.py's 'focal_length = b^2/(4|M|)' (composite.py:290-293). Also: concentric's measured conjugate points are for a POINT source 150 before the lens (A(0) = 0 at x0 = -150), so its 'f' column is the source-at-infinity figure, not the predicted conjugate; the thin-lens prediction 150 + f*150/(150-f) reproduces seats/none for all seven rows and the conjugate distances to within +1.2 to +3.5 (R7).

DISCREPANCY (composite.py VALIDATION 1, not an error in 4M/b) -- composite.py:42 'light deflection reproduces 4M/b to 0.03 % at b = 0.2' and composite.py:313-317. The validation run is FINITE (x0 = -4, lambda = 8, end x = 3.988) in the LINEARISED metric (composite.py:133-139, metric -(1+2Phi), (1-2Phi)). Finite-path Born gives bend/(4M/b) = 0.998749 at b = 0.2 and 0.999687 at b = 0.1; the linearised metric's second-order term (exact coefficient 4 pi, i.e. PPN beta = delta = 0, not Schwarzschild's 15 pi/4; R4) adds +pi M/b = +1.571e-3 and +3.142e-3. composite measures 1.000281 and 1.002826; the combined prediction is 1.000319 and 1.002828 (residuals -3.8e-5, -2.0e-6). So the pipeline is CONFIRMED to ~4e-5, but the quoted '0.03 %' is a near-cancellation of a -0.125 % truncation and a +0.157 % second-order term, each about five times the stated agreement; at b = 0.2 first-order finite-path alone would FAIL the selftest's 1e-3 tolerance. Recorded, not repaired.

DISCREPANCY (misprint-level) -- spec.py:65 docstring 'f = 8.1923e13 m' against spec.focal_length(1.989e30, 6.957e8) = 8.19191e13 m (relative 4.8e-5); the AU figure 547.6 on the same line and the selftest pin are consistent with the code.

DISCREPANCY (citation precision) -- spec.py:66, 281, 341 cite the published solar focus as '~550 AU' with no reference, and specthm.py:3568-3571 pins that 550 is NOT within spec's 1e-3 of f_sun (0.44 % apart, specthm.py:1324-1329). The published figure (Toth & Turyshev, WebSearch summary only, NOT READ) is ~547.8 AU; spec's own f_sun = 547.595 AU is 0.037 % from it, and the same formula with IAU 2015 nominal GM_sun gives 547.758 AU (0.008 %). If 547.8 is confirmed at source, the tree's recorded 'not within 1e-3' is an artefact of the rounded citation, not a disagreement with the literature.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0; output in rederive/weak-field-lens-focal-length.out). R1 sympy: Born integral of the linearised metric gives alpha = 4M/b exactly. R2 sympy: z_f = b/tan(4M/b) -> b^2/(4M), units -> b^2 c^2/(4GM); thin lens D_i = f D_s/(D_s-f) >= f, -> f as D_s -> infinity. R4 mpmath exact quadrature: Schwarzschild (alpha-4M/b)/(M/b)^2 = 11.785 at M/b = 1e-4 (15 pi/4 = 11.781); linearised isotropic metric 12.572 (4 pi = 12.566). lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. Einstein (1916) and Eddington (1919) lacked a precision value of gamma, and the 1919 eclipse data were ~20 % measurements; VLBI (restated in gr-qc/0003025, READ) later fixed the coefficient to (1+gamma)/2 = 1 within 1.6e-4, and Cassini (NAMED-NOT-READ) to ~1e-5 -- the later data CONFIRM the factor 4 rather than move it; f moves by <= 1.9e-4. They also lacked the modern GM_sun (IAU 2015, READ): using it moves the tree's solar focus by +3e-4 toward the published 547.8 AU. What earlier treatments lacked in the other sense -- wave optics and the solar corona -- is now in the literature (1810.06627, 1811.06515, NOT READ) and restricts WHERE the geodesic focus is a light focus (optical yes, radio pushed outward; a 10 km asteroid never, computed here), not the formula. Evidence against the hypothesis for this result: no datum that has moved moves f by more than 3e-4. Evidence for a weaker form: the geometric-optics and plasma-free conditions were implicit in the classic and are unnamed in the tree.
grade_evidence: The formula STANDS as mathematics: alpha = 4GM/(c^2 b) and f = b^2 c^2/(4GM) re-derived here from the linearised metric (sympy Born integral), with the second-order Schwarzschild correction 15 pi/4 (M/b)^2 confirmed by exact quadrature and shown to be 6e-6 at the solar limb; every moved datum (gamma, GM_sun, G, au) moves f by <= 3e-4, inside spec's own 1e-3 pin. It is NARROWED against the tree's use on one computed ground and one named one: (i) the tree reads the null-geodesic focus as physical focusing (spec.py:57-72, 194; specthm SR1 prints the asteroid row) without naming geometric optics; for the 10 km asteroid the on-axis wave gain at 500 nm is 1.00013 (R9) -- no light focus -- while the Sun (gain 2.3e11) and every load-bearing use (S-1 witness, SR1 for null geodesics, R5-S) are unaffected; (ii) 'through vacuum' at b = R_sun (specthm.py:1311-1317) is only approximately met by the Sun, with a frequency-dependent plasma effect named in 1811.06515 (NOT READ, not computed). Three discrepancies recorded, none an error: composite.py:42's '0.03 %' is a cancellation of finite-path truncation (-0.125 %) and the linearised metric's second-order term (+0.157 %), the pipeline itself agreeing with the correct prediction to 3.8e-5; spec.py:65 prints 8.1923e13 m for a computed 8.19191e13 m; spec.py:66's uncited '~550 AU' is 0.44 % from f_sun where the published ~547.8 AU (search summary, NOT READ) would be 0.037 %. The source itself was NOT READ (alphaXiv quota exceeded, arxiv egress-blocked): the grade rests on the re-derivation, not on a read.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names geometric optics (lambda << 4GM/c^2) and a frequency condition for the solar limb as hypotheses of SR1/spec's table, or restricts the 'focus' readings to null geodesics and drops the asteroid row as a physical focus. To OPEN/other: a READ of Einstein's statement or of a Turyshev-Toth paper that stated a different coefficient or focal figure (none expected; the re-derivation fixes both). Reading 1811.06515 at source would quantify the coronal shift and could move (ii) from named to computed. Nothing available here could make it WRONG: no counterexample exists in the weak-field, geometric-optics class.
